# OxidePM

> OxidePM is an open-source process manager written in Rust, for Linux. It starts apps, restarts them when they crash, keeps their logs and brings them back after a reboot. The language runtimes, notifications, the web API, the terminal dashboard and Prometheus metrics are adapters. Licensed MIT or Apache-2.0.

OxidePM 0.4.0-rc.6 bundles all 13 release adapters. On Linux, the install script enables only the four runtimes. macOS supports the built-in `cmd` runtime. The adapter launcher and sandbox are Linux-only in this release. Source: https://github.com/oxidekit/oxidepm.

`oxidepm update` verifies the release signature before downloading the archive. On Linux, restart the daemon after the upgrade and run `oxidepm adapter update --all` to refresh installed bundled adapters. The updater suggests this command starting with 0.4.0-rc.6. If you upgrade from an older CLI, run it yourself.

On Linux, install any adapter from the release with `oxidepm adapter import --bundled <name> --enable`. Review its permissions and confirm the grant at the prompt. If approval is deferred, use the printed `oxidepm adapter enable <name> --accept <fingerprint>` command after reviewing the grant. For a self-built adapter, import the archive with `oxidepm adapter import ./my-adapter.tar.gz --sha256 <digest> --enable`. Add `--allow-reserved-name` if it uses a reserved name.

## Getting started

- [Install](https://oxidepm.com/docs/getting-started/install.md): Install OxidePM with the install script, a package, a prebuilt archive or from source.
- [Your first app](https://oxidepm.com/docs/getting-started/first-app.md): Start an app, look at it, read its logs and stop it.
- [Survive a reboot](https://oxidepm.com/docs/getting-started/reboot.md): Save the app list, generate a boot unit and bring the apps back.
- [Upgrade](https://oxidepm.com/docs/getting-started/upgrade.md): Update to a newer release with oxidepm update, and what it checks.

## Configuration

- [The config file](https://oxidepm.com/docs/configuration/config-file.md): Where an app's settings live, which formats are read and how strictly.
- [Apps](https://oxidepm.com/docs/configuration/apps.md): Every key an app can have in a config file.
- [Restarts and states](https://oxidepm.com/docs/configuration/restarts.md): Restart policy, backoff, the crash-loop breaker and the states an app moves through.
- [Dependencies](https://oxidepm.com/docs/configuration/dependencies.md): Use depends_on to make an app wait for the apps it needs. A wait that fails closed.
- [Health checks](https://oxidepm.com/docs/configuration/health-checks.md): HTTP, TCP and script checks, and what the daemon does when one fails.
- [Limits and cron](https://oxidepm.com/docs/configuration/limits-and-cron.md): Restart an app over a memory or uptime limit, or on a cron schedule.
- [Clusters](https://oxidepm.com/docs/configuration/clusters.md): Run several instances of one app, with a port for each.
- [Log files](https://oxidepm.com/docs/configuration/log-files.md): Where an app's output goes, and how the files rotate.
- [Environment and hooks](https://oxidepm.com/docs/configuration/environment-and-hooks.md): What environment an app gets, how secrets are shown, and event hooks.
- [Daemon settings](https://oxidepm.com/docs/configuration/daemon-settings.md): The optional daemon.toml and the files in the data directory.

## Commands

- [Overview](https://oxidepm.com/docs/commands/overview.md): The core commands, selectors and global flags, the commands and runtimes that adapters provide, and what you see when one is missing.
- [start, stop, restart](https://oxidepm.com/docs/commands/start-stop-restart.md): Start an app or a config file, stop it, restart it, reload it and delete it.
- [status and show](https://oxidepm.com/docs/commands/status.md): Read what is running: the table, the extra columns, one app in detail and the daemon itself.
- [logs and flush](https://oxidepm.com/docs/commands/logs.md): Read, follow and filter an app's logs, and truncate them.
- [save and resurrect](https://oxidepm.com/docs/commands/save-and-resurrect.md): Write the list of apps that should run, and start them again.
- [Dry run](https://oxidepm.com/docs/commands/dry-run.md): Ask what a command would do and change nothing.
- [JSON output](https://oxidepm.com/docs/commands/json-output.md): The --json flag, and what it prints.
- [Error codes](https://oxidepm.com/docs/commands/error-codes.md): The stable E_ codes, where you can see them, and what they mean.
- [Other commands](https://oxidepm.com/docs/commands/other-commands.md): Update, backup and restore, env, top, completions, and the commands that adapters provide: web, monit, init, check, deploy and diff.

## Adapters

- [How adapters work](https://oxidepm.com/docs/adapters/how-adapters-work.md): What an adapter is, what runs where, and what happens when one fails.
- [Import and enable](https://oxidepm.com/docs/adapters/import-and-enable.md): Install an adapter from an archive you pin, read what it asks for, and enable it.
- [Permissions](https://oxidepm.com/docs/adapters/permissions.md): What a manifest can ask for, and what the daemon enforces itself.
- [The sandbox](https://oxidepm.com/docs/adapters/sandbox.md): Landlock and seccomp: what they limit, where they apply and where they stop.
- [The notifier](https://oxidepm.com/docs/adapters/notifier.md): Telegram, Discord, Slack and webhook notifications.
- [The Prometheus exporter](https://oxidepm.com/docs/adapters/exporter-prometheus.md): Prometheus metrics from the daemon's status, served by an adapter.

## AI safety

- [Agent connections](https://oxidepm.com/docs/ai-safety/agent-connections.md): How the daemon decides who is asking, and the agent socket.
- [Permission tiers](https://oxidepm.com/docs/ai-safety/permission-tiers.md): Safe, caution and dangerous requests, and what an AI actor may ask for.
- [Protected apps](https://oxidepm.com/docs/ai-safety/protected-apps.md): The protected and ai_control markers, and how to change them.
- [Audit log](https://oxidepm.com/docs/ai-safety/audit-log.md): What is written to the audit log, what is not, and how to read it.
- [Safe use with AI agents](https://oxidepm.com/docs/ai-safety/safe-use.md): A runbook: which commands are safe to let an agent run, and the mistakes agents make.

## Adapter protocol

- [Overview](https://oxidepm.com/docs/adapter-protocol/overview.md): Protocol version 1: transport, framing and the rules every message follows.
- [Messages](https://oxidepm.com/docs/adapter-protocol/messages.md): Every method the daemon and an adapter may send.
- [Handshake and lifecycle](https://oxidepm.com/docs/adapter-protocol/lifecycle.md): How an adapter starts, is checked and is stopped.
- [The host API](https://oxidepm.com/docs/adapter-protocol/host-api.md): How an adapter asks the daemon to do something, and what the grant allows.
- [Events](https://oxidepm.com/docs/adapter-protocol/events.md): The lifecycle and adapter event families, and how delivery works.
- [Limits and timeouts](https://oxidepm.com/docs/adapter-protocol/limits.md): The numbers the daemon enforces, and what happens when an adapter exceeds them.
- [Errors](https://oxidepm.com/docs/adapter-protocol/errors.md): Error codes in the protocol, and what fails closed or open.
- [Write an adapter](https://oxidepm.com/docs/adapter-protocol/write-an-adapter.md): The manifest file, the archive layout and a minimal adapter.

## Compare

- [OxidePM and PM2](https://oxidepm.com/docs/compare/oxidepm-and-pm2.md): What each process manager is for, where each is the better choice, and the real differences.
- [OxidePM and systemd](https://oxidepm.com/docs/compare/oxidepm-and-systemd.md): Where systemd is enough, where a process manager is easier, and how the two work together.
